packet.objective: Prove or refute the structural claims D1-D3 for S = {sorted positive-integer quadruples with a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2 = 4abcd} under Vieta mutation (replace one coordinate x_i by 4 times the product of the other three minus x_i, then re-sort): (D1) every solution is connected to the root (1,1,1,1) by a mutation path; (D2) every non-root vertex has a unique height-decreasing mutation, where height-decreasing means strictly decreasing the maximum coordinate d (coordinate sum only auxiliary); (D3) consequently the quotient mutation graph is a rooted tree. Suggested route, to be verified rigorously: at a non-root vertex show d^2 > a^2+b^2+c^2 (equivalently the Vieta conjugate d' = (a^2+b^2+c^2)/d = 4abc - d satisfies 1 <= d' < d), e.g. by showing d' >= d forces a=b=1 and then c^2 - 4cd + d^2 = -2, whose integer solutions are excluded by m^2 = 3c^2 + 2 being impossible mod 3 except at the root; show c = d occurs only at the root; show mutation at any coordinate < d strictly increases the maximum; conclude strict descent, termination at the root, uniqueness of the parent, and the tree property (a cycle would give its maximum-height vertex two distinct height-decreasing mutations). If any claim fails, exhibit and verify the failure structure.

Expected components, to be proved or improved: (i) every child of a non-root vertex has maximum at least 3 times the parent's maximum (since mutating at any coordinate below the maximum d gives a new value >= (4ab-1)d with ab >= 1), hence depth(v) <= log_3(max(v)) and max(v) >= 3^{depth(v)}; (ii) every non-root vertex has at most 3 children and the root has exactly 1, giving a crude N(H) = O(H); (iii) sharpen the O(H) bound as far as rigorously possible (e.g., by analyzing coincidences between children, forced sorting effects, or refined growth factors larger than 3 on most branches), and give a two-sided relation between depth and log H along extremal branches (fastest- and slowest-growing chains). No growth law may be assumed; every bound must come with explicit constants and complete proofs.
